From b11c81731c810efe592e510bb0110e0db6877419 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ravi Gunasekaran <r-gunasekaran@ti.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2024 15:34:47 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] net: hsr: hsr_slave: Fix the promiscuous mode in offload mode

commit e748d0fd66ab ("net: hsr: Disable promiscuous mode in
offload mode") disables promiscuous mode of slave devices
while creating an HSR interface. But while deleting the
HSR interface, it does not take care of it. It decreases the
promiscuous mode count, which eventually enables promiscuous
mode on the slave devices when creating HSR interface again.

Fix this by not decrementing the promiscuous mode count while
deleting the HSR interface when offload is enabled.

Fixes: e748d0fd66ab ("net: hsr: Disable promiscuous mode in offload mode")
Signed-off-by: Ravi Gunasekaran <r-gunasekaran@ti.com>
Reviewed-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@nvidia.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240322100447.27615-1-r-gunasekaran@ti.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/hsr/hsr_slave.c b/net/hsr/hsr_slave.c
index e5742f2a2d52..1b6457f357bd 100644
--- a/net/hsr/hsr_slave.c
+++ b/net/hsr/hsr_slave.c
@@ -220,7 +220,8 @@ void hsr_del_port(struct hsr_port *port)
 		netdev_update_features(master->dev);
 		dev_set_mtu(master->dev, hsr_get_max_mtu(hsr));
 		netdev_rx_handler_unregister(port->dev);
-		dev_set_promiscuity(port->dev, -1);
+		if (!port->hsr->fwd_offloaded)
+			dev_set_promiscuity(port->dev, -1);
 		netdev_upper_dev_unlink(port->dev, master->dev);
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/hsr/hsr_slave.c`**
- A conditional check was added to the function `hsr_del_port`. The line that decrements the promiscuous mode count (`dev_set_promiscuity(port->dev, -1);`) is now only executed if the `fwd_offloaded` flag of the `hsr` structure is false. This prevents the promiscuous mode count from being decremented when the HSR interface is being deleted and offload mode is enabled.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (`e748d0fd66ab`), which disabled promiscuous mode for slave devices in offload mode. The current patch ensures that the promiscuous mode count is not decremented during the deletion of the HSR interface when offload mode is enabled, thereby maintaining the intended behavior of the promiscuous mode across HSR interface operations.

Here is the commit message:
net: hsr: hsr_slave: Fix the promiscuous mode in offload mode

commit e748d0fd66ab ("net: hsr: Disable promiscuous mode in
offload mode") disables promiscuous mode of slave devices
while creating an HSR interface. But while deleting the
HSR interface, it does not take care of it. It decreases the
promiscuous mode count, which eventually enables promiscuous
mode on the slave devices when creating HSR interface again.

Fix this by not decrementing the promiscuous mode count while
deleting the HSR interface when offload is enabled.

Fixes: e748d0fd66ab ("net: hsr: Disable promiscuous mode in offload mode")
Signed-off-by: Ravi Gunasekaran <r-gunasekaran@ti.com>
Reviewed-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@nvidia.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240322100447.27615-1-r-gunasekaran@ti.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the improper handling of the promiscuous mode count during the deletion of the HSR interface. While the commit `e748d0fd66ab` correctly disables promiscuous mode for slave devices when the HSR interface is created, it fails to account for the scenario when the interface is deleted. As a result, the promiscuous mode count is decremented even when offload mode is enabled, which inadvertently re-enables promiscuous mode on the slave devices when the HSR interface is created again.

Here is the patch:
 
 void hsr_del_port(struct hsr_port *port)
 {
 	struct hsr_priv *hsr;
 	struct hsr_port *master;
 
 	hsr = port->hsr;
 	master = hsr_port_get_hsr(hsr, HSR_PT_MASTER);
 	list_del_rcu(&port->port_list);
 
 	if (port != master) {
 		netdev_update_features(master->dev);
 		dev_set_mtu(master->dev, hsr_get_max_mtu(hsr));
 		netdev_rx_handler_unregister(port->dev);
-		dev_set_promiscuity(port->dev, -1);
+		if (!port->hsr->fwd_offloaded)
+			dev_set_promiscuity(port->dev, -1);
 		netdev_upper_dev_unlink(port->dev, master->dev);
 	}
 
 	synchronize_rcu();
 
 	kfree(port);
 }
--

```c

```
Reason:
This statement decrements the promiscuous mode count for the slave device when the HSR interface is deleted, regardless of whether offload mode is enabled. This improper handling causes the promiscuous mode to be inadvertently re-enabled when the HSR interface is created again.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!port->hsr->fwd_offloaded)
    dev_set_promiscuity(port->dev, -1);
```
Reason:
This conditional check ensures that the promiscuous mode count is only decremented if offload mode is not enabled. By adding this check, the patch prevents the unintended re-enabling of promiscuous mode on the slave devices when the HSR interface is deleted, thus maintaining the intended behavior.
